memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the eighth day hold a closing special assembly and do no regular work. Present as an aroma pleasing to the LORD a food offering consisting of a burnt offering of one bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect. With the bull, the ram and the lambs, offer their grain offerings and drink offerings according to the number specified. Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering." - Num 29:35-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The festival closed with a special assembly on the eighth day, a fitting conclusion to this rich season of worship. After the abundance of the previous days, the offerings on this final day returned to a simpler form: one bull, one ram, seven lambs. It was a gathering to mark the completion of the feast, a closing act of devotion before the people returned to their ordinary lives.

There is something meaningful about this closing assembly. The season of intense worship did not simply trail off; it was brought to a deliberate and sacred close. God's people gathered one final time to worship before dispersing. The end of the feast was marked with the same care as its beginning.

This reminds us that our seasons of drawing near to God are meant to shape how we live afterward. The people would leave this assembly and return to their fields and homes, but they went out having been with God. Times of concentrated worship are meant to send us back into daily life renewed and refreshed in the Lord.

It was during this very feast, on the last and greatest day, that Jesus stood and called out an invitation to all who were thirsty to come to Him (John 7:37). The feast pointed to Him, the fountain of living water. As we conclude times of worship, we go out carrying Christ with us into ordinary life. Let every gathering with God send you back renewed to live for Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do your times of worship shape how you live afterward?
2. Do you return to daily life carrying what you received from God?
3. What does it mean that Jesus is the living water this feast pointed to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my times of drawing near to You shape how I live afterward. Send me back into ordinary life renewed, carrying Christ the living water with me into every day. Amen.
